title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement:
Given an unsorted array of integers `nums`, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence.

You must write an algorithm that runs in **O(n)** time.

Put every number into a hash set, then only start counting a sequence from numbers that are the *start* of a run (i.e., `num - 1` is not in the set). This avoids re-scanning the same run multiple times.

examples.explanation: The longest consecutive sequence is [1,2,3,4], so the length is 4.

editorial.approach: Insert every number into a hash set to allow O(1) lookups and remove duplicates. For each number that is the start of a sequence (meaning `num - 1` is not in the set), walk forward counting how many consecutive numbers (`num`, `num + 1`, `num + 2`, ...) are also in the set, tracking the longest run found. Because only sequence starts trigger a walk, each number is visited at most twice overall, giving O(n) time.
